title: Osmosis and Tonicity
short: Water moves across a membrane toward the side with more solute. In a hypotonic solution a cell gains water; in a hypertonic one it loses water; in an isotonic one there is no net change.
trouble: Students think solute moves rather than water, or mix up hypertonic and hypotonic. Compare the solution to the cell: hyper means more solute outside, so water leaves the cell.

blocks.html: Water diffuses too. When a membrane lets water through but not a dissolved substance (a solute), the water does all the moving. This special case of Diffusion and Concentration Gradients is osmosis, and it decides whether a cell swells, shrinks or stays the same.

In osmosis, water moves across a membrane toward the side with more solute (and so less free water). In a hypotonic solution a cell gains water; in a hypertonic one it loses water; in an isotonic one there is no net change.

blocks.name: bi-membrane
blocks.cap: The solute cannot cross; water moves toward the side with more solute.

blocks.html: Solute particles hold water molecules around them, so a solution with more solute has fewer free water molecules. Water diffuses from where free water is more concentrated (less solute) to where it is less concentrated (more solute). The words compare the solution outside with the cell: hyper means more, hypo less, iso equal.

head: Solution outside
Animal cell
Plant cell
blocks.cap: Always compare the solution outside with the cell. A plant cell's wall keeps it from bursting; in a hypertonic solution the plant wilts.

blocks.name: bi-membrane
blocks.cap: Switch between hypotonic, isotonic and hypertonic to see the cell change.

blocks.title: Name the solution
blocks.q: A red blood cell is about 0.9% salt inside. It is put into 3% salt water. Is the solution hypotonic, isotonic or hypertonic, and what happens?
steps: Compare outside with inside: $3\% > 0.9\%$, so the solution has more solute.
Water moves out toward the extra solute, and the cell shrivels.
blocks.a: Hypertonic; the cell loses water and shrivels.

blocks.title: Potato data
blocks.q: Potato cubes gain 6% mass in 0.1 M sugar and lose 4% in 0.4 M. Between which concentrations is the solution isotonic to the potato cells, and about where?
steps: Gaining mass means water went in: 0.1 M is hypotonic. Losing mass means 0.4 M is hypertonic.
Isotonic is where the change is zero, between them.
On a straight line from +6% to −4%, zero lies $\frac{6}{10}$ of the way: $0.1 + 0.6 \times 0.3 = 0.28$ M.

blocks.html: Thinking the solute moves instead of the water, or mixing up hyper and hypo. In osmosis the solute stays put; water moves toward it. To keep the words straight, compare the solution to the cell: hyper means more solute outside, so water leaves the cell. A memory aid: in a hypotonic solution the cell swells up like an "o".
